newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates up on pest damage fears.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates up on pest damage fears.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates jumped on Wednesday on talk of pest damage to the crop, even though government officials insisted that losses were limited, dealers said.

"Despite official denial, spinners are scared by the rumours and are picking up whatever was available," dealer Mustafa Hussain said, adding that the market would remain volatile unless a clear picture emerged.
Officials said crop damage was limited and the output target of 10 million 375-lb bales set for fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) would be achieved.
In the kerb market dealers said NIAB-78 variety rose 50 rupees ($1.34) to 2,200 per maund (37.32 kg).
